samples.summary: Introduces a third, global mechanism for the same "toolbar button must not hold the keyboard" problem the repo already solves per-control
samples.evidence: The repo already has two established patterns for exactly this concern: (a) `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` on toolbar toggles so focus never leaves the canvas/textarea (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:168,186`), and (b) `useMenuCloseHandlers(releaseFocusToBody)` wired into every slides palette/dropdown (`slides/toolbar/shape-controls.tsx:60`, `border-picker.tsx:72`, `text-element-controls.tsx:62`, `table-controls.tsx:103`, `fill-picker/gradient-editor.tsx:307`), documented at length in `packages/frontend/src/components/menu-focus.ts:3-30`. This diff adds a document-level capture-phase `pointerdown`/`keydown`/`focusin` listener that blankets the whole toolbar instead of extending or consolidating those. The two systems now overlap and can contend (e.g. `useMenuCloseHandlers(() => editor?.focus())` deliberately restores caret focus on swatch close while the new deferred timer independently re-reads `document.activeElement` and may blur). The design doc addition does not explain why the existing per-control mechanism was insufficient or why the palettes' handlers are not folded into the new hook.

samples.summary: `CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR` is exported as the opt-in API but no consumer uses it; the attribute is hardcoded at the call site
samples.evidence: `export const CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR = "data-canvas-toolbar"` is only referenced inside its own module (`TOOLBAR_SELECTOR`); `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110` writes the literal `data-canvas-toolbar=""` and the doc comment rationalises this with "a computed key does not type-check as a JSX spread" (a spread of `{[CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR]: ""}` in fact does). The exported constant therefore buys no coupling safety and is a dead export (also a knip unused-export risk).

samples.summary: Hook is called unconditionally, installing three document-level capture listeners even on the mobile branch where no element carries the opt-in attribute
samples.evidence: `useCanvasFocusRelease()` runs before the `if (isMobile) return <MobileSlidesToolbar .../>` early return (index.tsx:92-107), and `MobileSlidesToolbar` never sets `data-canvas-toolbar` — the mobile toolbar is explicitly out of scope per `docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:56`. The listeners are then pure overhead on mobile. A scoped alternative (ref on the toolbar root, listeners on that element) would also avoid document-wide capture entirely.

samples.summary: The release is mode-agnostic: it also arms while the toolbar is in text-edit mode, where dropping focus to `document.body` would blur/commit the active text box
samples.evidence: `SlidesToolbar` renders `TextEditSection` inside the same `<Toolbar data-canvas-toolbar="">` root (index.tsx:136-138), so a pointer-driven focusin on any of those controls schedules `releaseFocusToBody()`. Correctness today depends on every text-edit control either preventing focus on mousedown or ending with `textEditor.focus()` (e.g. `text-edit-section.tsx:75,79`, `text-format-group.tsx:154`) — an invariant the hook itself does not enforce or check. The hook has no notion of the editor's mode, so any future text-edit control that forgets to refocus silently exits text editing rather than merely failing to release.

verdict.reason:
The duplication/overlap described is not present as claimed.

1) The new hook does not reinvent the existing helper — it *imports and reuses* it: `packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.ts:2` (`import { releaseFocusToBody } from "./menu-focus"`) and calls it at line 104. There is no second copy of the blur logic (`.blur()` on `document.activeElement` exists only at `menu-focus.ts:70`; a repo-wide grep for `focusin`/`.blur()` in `packages/frontend/src` finds no other global focus-release mechanism).

2) Neither claimed "established pattern" covers the case the hook addresses, so this is not a third mechanism for an already-solved problem:
   - `useMenuCloseHandlers` is scoped to *controlled colour-palette dropdowns* and, by its own documented design (`menu-focus.ts:20-29`, `52-57`), deliberately fires **only** on a swatch click and lets outside-click/Esc fall through to Radix's focus-to-trigger. The failure in issue #882 (Radix returning focus to the trigger on Esc/outside close, and plain buttons keeping focus) is exactly the path it intentionally does not handle — see the passing behaviour asserted in `toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:61-74`.
   - `onMouseDown preventDefault` exists only in the docs rich-text controls (`text-format-group.tsx:168,186,204,223,286`, `text-paragraph-group.tsx`, `font-size-picker.tsx`). A grep of `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/**` for `onMouseDown`/`preventDefault` finds none on slides toolbar buttons (undo/redo, format painter, slide group, arrange triggers rendered at `slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110-154`), so that per-control pattern is not applied on this surface at all.

3) The concrete contention example is guarded: the deferred check only acts when `isReleasable()` is true, which requires `tagName === "BUTTON"` or `role="button"` (`toolbar-focus-release.ts:55-62`, `103-105`). After `useMenuCloseHandlers(() => editor?.focus())` focus sits on the hidden textarea, so the release is a no-op; and the toggles in `text-format-group.tsx` prevent focus from reaching the button in the first place. This is stated in the design doc (`docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:157-160`).

4) Design-doc discipline is satisfied, not violated: the rule is folded into the canonical subsystem doc (`docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:136-165`), which is linked from `docs/design/README.md:72` — no parallel doc. That section, plus `docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:8-35`, does explain the gap in the existing mechanism (the gate must hold only for the duration of the interaction; Radix hands focus back to the trigger) and explicitly reuses `releaseFocusToBody()`.

What remains of the finding is a preference that the palette handlers be consolidated into the new hook; under this lens that is taste/refactor (minor) and does not block, and no acceptance criterion or Non-Goal is cited against it.
